title: Support probability from Fourier degree
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$ be nonzero with Fourier degree at most $k$. Under the uniform distribution on the sign cube, the probability that $f$ is nonzero is at least $2^{-k}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
the Fourier degree of $f$ is at most $k$
